scenes.en: It's probably a stye. Here's what to do.
scenes.say: A painful red bump on your eyelid? It's probably a stye. Here's what to do, and what not to do.

scenes.en: A tiny oil gland at the lash line gets blocked and infected.
scenes.ta: இமை முடி அருகே உள்ள எண்ணெய் சுரப்பி அடைபடுகிறது
scenes.say: Your eyelids have tiny oil glands near the lashes. When one gets blocked and infected by germs, it swells into a stye.

scenes.en: Clean warm cloth, 10 minutes, 3–4 times a day
scenes.say: Do use a warm compress. A clean, warm cloth on the closed eye for about ten minutes, three or four times a day.

scenes.en: Clean hands before touching your eyes.
scenes.say: Do wash your hands before touching your eyes, and keep the eyelid gently clean.
Don't squeeze it or pop it. Squeezing can push the infection deeper, and spread it.

scenes.en: No eye makeup or contact lenses until it heals.
scenes.ta: குணமாகும் வரை மேக்கப், காண்டாக்ட் லென்ஸ் வேண்டாம்
scenes.say: Don't wear eye makeup or contact lenses until it heals.

scenes.en: Swelling spreads, the eye shuts, vision changes, or no better in a week
scenes.say: See a doctor if the swelling spreads across the eyelid or cheek, if the eye swells shut, if your vision changes, or if it's not better in about a week.

scenes.en: Most styes settle on their own in about a week.
scenes.say: Did you know? Most styes settle on their own in about a week. Keep getting them? Book an eye test to check for eye strain.
